sentences.text: Heard the parties.

2. This Criminal Miscellaneous Petition has been filed invoking the jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure with a prayer to quash the First Information Report and/ or any subsequent proceedings in connection with Itki P.S. Case No.86 of 2021 registered for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code which is now pending before the learned Judicial Magistrate-1st Class at Ranchi.

3. The allegation against the petitioner is that the petitioner along with the co-accused Ayan Kerketta has taken Rs.3,11,000/- from the informant for selling a land but did not sell the land and a cheque of Rs.1,00,000/- was given by the petitioner which was dishonoured.
Notice was given to the petitioner.
The petitioner did not pay the money.
Hence, alleging commission of the offence of cheating and criminal breach of trust, the F.I.R. of the case was registered.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner draws the attention of this Court towards page-21-25 of the brief which is the copy of the alleged agreement enclosed with the F.I.R. and submits that the same is an agreement between the informant and the co-accused Ayan Kerketta only but the same nowhere shows any involvement of the petitioner and drawing attention of this Court to page- 26-27 of the brief which is the copy of the legal notice issued by the informant to the co-accused Ayan Kerketta, which was also annexed with the F.I.R., learned counsel for the petitioner submits that there is absolutely no notice issued to the petitioner nor complaint under Section 138 N.I. 5.

Learned counsel for the petitioner relies upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of A.M. Mohan vs. The State Represented by SHO & Another reported in 2024 INSC 233 paragraph-13 of which reads as under:-
"13.

sentences.text: It could thus be seen that for attracting the provision of Section 420 of IPC, the FIR/complaint must show that the ingredients of Section 415 of IPC are made out and the person cheated must have been dishonestly induced to deliver the property to any person; or to make, alter or destroy valuable security or anything signed or sealed and capable of being converted into valuable security.

and submits that even if the allegations made in the F.I.R. or the documents enclosed with the F.I.R.
are considered to be true in their entirety, still the offence punishable either under Section 420 or 406 of the Indian Penal Code is not made out.

It is next submitted that continuation of the First Information Report and/ or any subsequent proceedings in connection with Itki P.S. Case No.86 of 2021 which is now pending before the learned Judicial Magistrate-1st Class at Ranchi, against the petitioner, will amount to abuse of process of law.
It is lastly submitted that thus the prayer, as made in this Cr.M.P., be allowed.

6. Learned Addl.P.P. appearing for the State submits that though in the F.I.R. specific allegation against the petitioner is that he is the person who also took money and issued a cheque and thereby committed the offence of cheating and criminal breach of trust but the learned Additional Public Prosecutor fairly submits that in the agreement annexed with the F.I.R. is between the informant and the co-accused Ayan Kerketta and nowhere the name of the petitioner is appearing therein and the legal notice was also issued to the co-accused Ayan Kerketta and the name of the petitioner is also not appearing in that notice but it is submitted that there is direct allegation against the petitioner.
Hence, it is submitted that this Cr.M.P., being without any merit, be dismissed.

7. Having heard the rival submissions made at the Bar and after carefully going through the materials available in the record, it is pertinent to mention here that in order to constitute the offence punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, it has to be shown that the accused had the intention to deceive since the beginning and the same is a sine qua non for committing the offence punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code and if the intention to deceive Shiv Prasad Kerketta Aged About 30 Years ... vs The State Of Jharkhand ...

2 develops later, the same will not amount to the offence of cheating punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code as has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Uma Shankar Gopalika vs. State of Bihar & Another reported in (2005) 10 SCC 336 paragraph-6 of which

entities.text: Uma Shankar Gopalika vs. State of Bihar & Another reported in (2005) 10 SCC 336
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: reads as under:-
6. "Xxxx xxxx xxxx

It is well settled that every breach of contract would not give rise to an offence of cheating and only in those cases breach of contract would amount to cheating where there was any deception played at the very inception.
If the intention to cheat has developed later on, the same cannot amount to cheating.

In the present case it has nowhere been stated that at the very inception there was any intention on behalf of the accused persons to cheat which is a condition precedent for an offence under Section 420 IPC."
(Emphasis supplied)

8. So far as the offence punishable under Section 406 of the Indian Penal Code is concerned, it is a settled principle of law as has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Binod Kumar & Others vs. State of Bihar & Another reported in (2014) 10 SCC 663 that to make out a case of criminal breach of trust, it is not sufficient to show that money has been retained by the accused persons

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
; it must also be shown that the accused persons dishonestly disposed of the same in some way or dishonestly retained the same; as has been observed in paragraph-18 of the case of Binod Kumar & Others vs. State of Bihar & Another (supra) which reads as under:-
"18.

entities.text: Binod Kumar & Others vs. State of Bihar & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the present case, looking at the allegations in the complaint on the face of it,
we find that no allegations are made attracting the ingredients of Section 405 IPC.

Likewise, there are no allegations as to cheating or the dishonest intention of the appellants in retaining the money in order to have wrongful gain to themselves or causing wrongful loss to the complainant.

Excepting the bald allegations that the appellants did not make payment to the second respondent and that the appellants utilised the amounts either by themselves or for some other work, there is no iota of allegation as to the dishonest intention in misappropriating the property.
To make out a case of criminal breach of trust, it is not sufficient to show that money has been retained by the appellants.
It must also be shown that the appellants dishonestly disposed of the same in some way or dishonestly retained the same.
The mere fact that the appellants did not pay the money to the complainant does not amount to criminal breach of trust."
(Emphasis supplied)

9. Now, coming to the facts of the case, there is no allegation against the petitioner of playing deception against the informant since the beginning of the transaction nor is there any allegation of dishonest misappropriation of any property by the petitioner.

Though in the F.I.R. it has been alleged that the petitioner was entrusted with the money but the agreement which was annexed with the F.I.R. by the informant herself, goes to show that the agreement was between the informant and the co-accused Ayan Kerketta and the same is also crystal clear from the legal notice issued on behalf of the informant.

sentences.text: Under such circumstances, this Court is of the considered view that even if the entire allegations made against the petitioner are considered to be true in their entirety, still neither the offence punishable under Section 420 nor the offence punishable under Section 406 of the Indian Penal Code is made out against the petitioner and continuation of this criminal proceeding against the petitioner will amount to abuse of process of law and this is a fit case where the First Information Report and subsequent proceedings in connection with Itki P.S. Case No.86 of 2021 which is now pending before the learned Judicial Magistrate-1st Class at Ranchi, be quashed and set aside.

11. Accordingly, the First Information Report and subsequent proceedings in connection with Itki P.S. Case No.86 of 2021 which is now pending before the learned Judicial Magistrate-1st Class at Ranchi, is quashed and set aside against the petitioner.
12. In the result, this Cr.M.P. stands allowed.
